geometry_edits.rationale: Reduce the bend so the dominant mass stays calmer and reads as one continuous neighborhood bar.
Push the cantilever farther into a clearer upper gesture while preserving the dominant base.
Add a true public void tied to the dominant mass to repair the weak frontage threshold.
Size the courtyard as a usable ground-space figure rather than a decorative subtraction.
Open the new courtyard toward the verified access side to strengthen public threshold logic.
Make the courtyard the organizing root so the hall/bar remains in its ancestry while the public void becomes primary.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the primary mass into a more legible active-bar datum before carving the public edge.
Keep the dominant bar aligned to preserve the readable long-side urban datum.
Reorient the carved void toward the verified access side to create a clearer public threshold.
Enlarge the carve so it reads as usable ground space rather than a minor nick.
Increase spatial depth of the entry court/void to improve publicness and legibility.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass in all four views, and its bent/cantilevered bar has acceptable continuity and parcel response. However, the public-threshold condition is weak: the visible ground response near the verified access edge is mostly sealed/opaque rather than a clearly legible court, notch, or open entry seam. The stepped/terraced top is not incoherent, but it is modestly arbitrary relative to the program, since it does not convincingly produce usable public void or a stronger mixed-use ground hierarchy. Overall the form is structurally coherent and not over-clipped, but it does not yet support the neighborhood-living brief strongly enough to pass program fit.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked mixed-use massing with a clear base-to-top hierarchy and a legible compressed/expanded section logic.
